questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively. Position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin.]

Two particles, $A$ and $B$, are moving on a smooth horizontal surface.
Each particle is moving with constant velocity.

At time $t$ seconds, the position vector of $A$ is given by $\mathbf{r}$ metres.

$\bullet$ When $t=2$, $\mathbf{r}=(-5\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j})$
$\bullet$ When $t=5$, $\mathbf{r}=(10\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$, the velocity of $A$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Use of $\frac{1}{3}(10\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}-(-5\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j}))$ (Condone subtraction in the wrong order and missing brackets)
A1: $=(5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ Correct only
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow column vectors throughout apart from in the answers to (a) and (b).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find an expression for $\mathbf{r}$ at time $t$ seconds.
Give your answer in the form $p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j}$, where $p$ and $q$ are functions of $t$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\{-5\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j}-2(5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\}+t(5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$ OR $\{10\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}-5(5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\}+t(5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$ Any equivalent unsimplified form using their $\mathbf{v}$, with correct structure
A1: $=(-15+5t)\mathbf{i}+(24-4t)\mathbf{j}$ Correct simplified form

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $t$ seconds, the position vector of $B$ is given by $\mathbf{s}$ metres where

$\mathbf{s}=-5\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j}+t(2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$

(c) Find, to the nearest degree, the bearing of $B$ from $A$ when $t=5$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Finding $\overrightarrow{AB}$ (or $\overrightarrow{BA}$) at $t=5$ ($\overrightarrow{AB}=-5\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j}$). Seen or implied, allow slips. Must use given $\mathbf{r}$ at $t=5$.
M1: e.g. $\theta=\tan^{-1}(\pm\frac{5}{12})$ or $\tan^{-1}(\pm\frac{12}{5})$ or $\sin^{-1}(\pm\frac{5}{13})$ or $\sin^{-1}(\pm\frac{12}{13})$ etc. Correct use of trig to find a relevant angle, using their $\overrightarrow{AB}$ or $\overrightarrow{BA}$, seen or implied
A1: Bearing $203(^\circ)$ Correct only, to nearest degree.

questions.stem:
A particle is projected vertically upwards with speed $U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $A$.

The point $A$ is 12 m vertically above the point $B$.

Point $B$ is on horizontal ground.

The particle moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground at $B$.

The time taken for the particle to travel from $A$ to $B$ is 4 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Use suvat to form an equation in $U$ only. Condone sign errors
A1: $-12=4U-\frac{1}{2}g\times16$ Correct unsimplified equation in $U$ only
A1: Obtain $U=16.6$ or $U=17$ Correct answer only. A0 for $2g-3$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the speed of the particle as it hits the ground at $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Use suvat to form an equation in the speed or the velocity only. Condone sign errors. N.B. Allow this mark, even if the $U$ that was found in (a) came from an incorrect method.
A1: e.g. $12=4v-\frac{1}{2}g\times16$ OR $-v=16.6-4g$ OR $v=\sqrt{16.6^2+2g\times12}$ OR $12=\frac{(-16.6+v)}{2}\times4$ OR $h=\frac{16.6^2}{2g}$ and $v=\sqrt{2g\times(h+12)}$ Correct unsimplified equation in the speed or the velocity only. Allow $\pm v$
A1: speed $=22.6$ or $23\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ Correct answer only, must be positive. A0 for $2g+3$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the particle from the instant it leaves $A$ to the instant it reaches $B$. (No further calculations are required.)
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1: Correct V shape with a longer 2nd line and the vertex on the $t$-axis. Two lines with gradients of (roughly) equal magnitude. B0 if a continuous vertical line at $t=4$
B1ft: Values 4 and their 16.6 and 22.6 marked correctly. Dependent on the correct shape, a longer 2nd line and the vertex on the $t$-axis and two lines with gradients of (roughly) equal magnitude.

questions.stem:
Two ropes are attached to a point on the front of a barge.
The barge is being pulled horizontally in a straight line along the centre of a long straight canal.

One rope makes an angle of $25^\circ$ with the direction of motion of the barge and has a tension of 800 N.
The other rope makes an angle of $\alpha^\circ$ with the direction of motion of the barge and has a tension of 500 N, as shown in Figure 2.

Both ropes are horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Resolve perpendicular to the direction of motion to form an equation in $\alpha$ only. Dimensionally correct. Both forces resolved. Condone sign errors. Condone sine/cosine confusion but M0 for $800\cos25^\circ+500\cos\alpha^\circ=0$ if clearly resolving in the direction of motion. OR sine rule on a vector triangle.
A1: $800\sin25^\circ=500\sin\alpha^\circ$ oe Correct unsimplified equation
A1: 43 or better (must be correctly rounded to however many figs they choose); $\alpha=42.5465\ldots$ is A0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The mass of the barge is 15 tonnes and the resistance to the motion of the barge is a constant force of magnitude 750 N.

(b) Find the acceleration of the barge.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Use $F=ma$ parallel to the direction of the motion, to form an equation in $\alpha$ and $a$ only. Dimensionally correct. Both forces resolved. Condone sine/cosine confusion. Condone sign errors. All relevant terms. Condone 15 or incorrect zeros for the mass. N.B. The resultant of the two tensions may be found using the sine rule or cosine rule on a vector triangle. N.B. An extra $g$ in a resolution is counted as an A error not an M error.
A1: $800\cos25^\circ+500\cos\alpha^\circ-750=15000a$ OR $\frac{500\sin(180^\circ-25^\circ-\alpha^\circ)}{\sin25^\circ}-750=15000a$ OR $\frac{800\sin(180^\circ-25^\circ-\alpha^\circ)}{\sin\alpha^\circ}-750=15000a$ OR $F-750=15000a$ where $F=\sqrt{800^2+500^2-2\times800\times500\cos(180^\circ-25^\circ-\alpha^\circ)}$ Unsimplified equation with at most one error.
A1: Correct unsimplified equation. $\alpha$ does not need to be substituted. N.B. If they haven't attempted part (a) and use a 'random' numerical value for $\alpha$, can score max A1A0. N.B. Allow $a$ replaced by $-a$
A1: Accept $0.023\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ or better, (must be correctly rounded to however many figs they choose); $a=0.02289\ldots$ is A0. N.B. Penalise the use of $\ldots$ in their answer, ONCE for the question.

questions.stem:
A non-uniform rod $AB$ of length $3a$ rests in equilibrium on a horizontal ledge and overhangs the edge of the ledge at $C$.
The point $C$ is such that $AC=2a$ and $CB=a$, as shown in Figure 3.

The rod has weight $W$.

The distance of the centre of mass of the rod from $A$ is $d$.

The rod is perpendicular to the edge of the ledge.

When a force of magnitude $P$, **acting vertically upwards**, is applied to the rod at $B$, the rod is on the point of tilting about $A$.

When the force applied at $B$ is replaced by a force of magnitude $1.25P$, **acting vertically downwards** at $B$, the rod is on the point of tilting about $C$.

Find $d$ in terms of $a$.

parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of sufficient equations to form an equation in $a$, $d$, $P$ and $W$ only. M(A) OR $\{F=0, E+P=W$ and M(C), M(B), or M(G)$\}$. All equations dimensionally correct with correct no. of terms. N.B. Must be using $P$ in this case, unless a clear misread. M(C): $aP+W(2a-d)=2aE$; M(B): $3aE=(a+2a-d)W$; M(G): $P(a+2a-d)=dE$
A1: $3aP=dW$ Correct unsimplified equation in $a$, $d$, $P$ and $W$ only
M1: Use of sufficient equations to form another equation in $a$, $d$, $P$ and $W$ only. M(C) OR $\{G=0, H=1.25P+W$ and M(A), M(B), or M(G)$\}$. All equations dimensionally correct with correct no. of terms. N.B. Must be using $1.25P$ in this case, unless a clear misread. M(A): $Wd+3a\times1.25P=2aH$; M(B): $aH=(a+2a-d)W$; M(G): $1.25P(a+2a-d)=(2a-d)H$
A1: $1.25Pa=W(2a-d)$ Correct unsimplified equation in $a$, $d$, $P$ and $W$ only
DM1: Solve for $d$ in terms of $a$. Complete method. Dependent on the two preceding M marks
A1: Obtain $(d=)\frac{24a}{17}$ Accept $d=1.4a$ or better ($d=1.41176\ldots a$) but NOT $\frac{6a}{4.25}$ or similar. N.B. If $W$ is replaced by say, $Mg$ or $M$ etc, can score all the marks but if they use $Wg$ with $P$ in their equations, can score max M1A0M1A0DM1A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. Enter marks on ePEN for the two equations in the same order as they appear in the MS.

questions.stem:
Figure 4 shows a rough plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\theta=\frac{3}{4}$

The points $A$ and $B$ lie on a line of greatest slope of the plane, with $B$ above $A$.

A package $P$ of mass $m$ is projected up the plane from $A$ towards $B$.

The coefficient of friction between the plane and the package is $\frac{1}{4}$

The package $P$ is modelled as a particle.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the **deceleration** of $P$, as it moves from $A$ to $B$, is $\frac{4}{5}g$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Resolve perpendicular to the slope: $R=mg\cos\theta\,(=\frac{4}{5}mg)$ OR $R=W\cos\theta\,(=\frac{4}{5}W)$. Condone sine/cosine confusion and use of $\alpha$, or similar, for $\theta$
M1: Use of $F=\frac{1}{4}R$. $R$ does not need to be substituted.
A1: Friction $=\frac{1}{4}\times mg\cos\theta$ Seen or implied.
M1: Equation of motion. $F+mg\sin\theta=ma$ OR $F+W\sin\theta=\frac{W}{g}a$. Need all 3 terms. Condone sign errors and sine/cosine confusion
A1: Correct unsimplified equation. Allow with $-a$
A1*: $(a=)\frac{4}{5}g$ Given answer. A0 for $0.8g$. If using $-a$, allow $-a=\frac{4}{5}g$ but not $a=-\frac{4}{5}g$ as the final answer. N.B. Full marks available if $m$ replaced with 2 throughout. N.B. The first 3 marks are for finding the friction and just stating that $F=\frac{1}{5}mg$, scores M0M0A0. N.B. Since this is a 'Show that…' question the final A1* can only be scored for a fully correct solution, including use of $\cos\theta=\frac{4}{5}$ and $\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The package $P$ comes to rest at $B$.

Given that $P$ is projected from $A$ with speed $U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and that $AB=1.5$ m,

(b) find the value of $U$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Use of suvat to form an equation in $U$ only. e.g. $0=U^2-2\times\frac{4}{5}g\times1.5$. N.B. Must use $a=\pm\frac{4}{5}g$
A1: Obtain $U=4.8$ or $U=4.85$ 2 sf or 3 sf only. Not $\sqrt{\frac{12}{5}g}$ nor $\frac{14\sqrt{3}}{5}$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
On reaching $B$, $P$ is held at rest there by a force of magnitude $X$ newtons acting up the plane in the direction $AB$.

Given that the mass of $P$ is 2 kg,

(c) find the smallest possible value of $X$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Resolve parallel to the slope: $X+F=2g\sin\theta$. Correct terms. M0 if using $R$ in their equation. Condone sign errors and sine/cosine confusion. N.B. Allow $m$ for the mass.
A1: $X+\frac{1}{4}\times2g\cos\theta=2g\sin\theta$ Correct unsimplified equation in $X$ and $\theta$
A1: $X=\frac{4}{5}g=7.8$ or 7.84. 2 sf or 3 sf only. Allow $\frac{4}{5}g$ or 0.8g

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors.]

Two boats, $A$ and $B$, are each moving with constant acceleration.

At time $t$ hours after noon, boat $A$ has velocity $\mathbf{v}_A\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$, where

$\mathbf{v}_A=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+(\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})t$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $A$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $|\mathbf{a}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-4)^2}$ or $\sqrt{1^2+4^2}$. Complete method to find the magnitude using the correct vector or the correct vector with just a sign error. They may use $\mathbf{a}=\frac{\mathbf{v}_p-\mathbf{v}_q}{p-q}$ for two specific times $p$ and $q$, allow subtraction either way round and slips in arithmetic
A1: $=\sqrt{17}$. Accept $4.1\,(\mathrm{km\,h^{-2}})$ or better; $=4.123105\ldots\,(\mathrm{km\,h^{-2}})$ Must come from a correct $\mathbf{a}$ (if seen).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow column vectors throughout apart from in the answers to (b) and (c).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
When $t=2$, the velocity of $B$ is $(4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

When $t=5$, the velocity of $B$ is $(\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

(b) Find the acceleration of $B$, giving your answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\frac{(\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})-(4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})}{3}$ Condone subtraction the wrong way round
A1: $=-\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{km\,h^{-2}})$ Must be in $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the velocity of $B$ at time $t=0$, giving your answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}-2(-\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$ OR $\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}-5(-\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$. Or equivalent for their $\mathbf{a}$
A1: $=6\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}})$ Must be in $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$. Isw if they find the speed. N.B. In (b) and (c), penalise the use of column vectors in the answers ONCE.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
At time $T_1$ hours after noon, both boats are moving with the same speed.

(d) Find the exact value of $T_1$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: Express both velocities in component form, with $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s collected, using their answers to (b) and (c) for $\mathbf{v}_B$. $\mathbf{v}_A=(2+t)\mathbf{i}+(3-4t)\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{v}_B=(6-t)\mathbf{i}+(5-2t)\mathbf{j}$. Seen or implied. Allow slips. N.B. This mark can be earned in part (e).
M1: Correct use of Pythagoras to form an equation in $T_1$ (or $t$) only, with or without square roots. For given $\mathbf{v}_A$ and their $\mathbf{v}_B$
A1ft: $(6-T_1)^2+(5-2T_1)^2=(2+T_1)^2+(3-4T_1)^2$ $(T_1^2+T_1-4=0)$ Correct unsimplified equation in $T_1$ (or $t$), without square roots. Follow their answers from (b) and (c)
A1: $\frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}{2}$ only cao accept exact equivalent

parts.label: e
parts.text:
At time $T_2$ hours after noon, both boats are moving in the same direction.

(e) Show that $3T_2^2+pT_2+q=0$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) M1: Use ratios to form an equation in $T_2$ (or $t$) only. Allow reciprocal on one side. N.B. Allow if $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s are left in
A1ft: $\frac{5-2T_2}{6-T_2}=\frac{3-4T_2}{2+T_2}$ (allow $t$ at this stage) Or equivalent. ft on their $\mathbf{v}_B$
A1*: $\Rightarrow3T_2^2-14T_2+4=0$ Obtain correct answer from full and correct working with no errors. Must see at least $10+5T_2-4T_2-2T_2^2=18-24T_2-3T_2+4T_2^2$ OR $10+T_2-2T_2^2=18-27T_2+4T_2^2$ (Allow $t$ at this stage but must be $T_2$ in final answer) $\Rightarrow3T_2^2-14T_2+4=0$

questions.question_text:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors.]

Two boats, $A$ and $B$, are each moving with constant acceleration.

At time $t$ hours after noon, boat $A$ has velocity $\mathbf{v}_A\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$, where

$\mathbf{v}_A=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+(\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})t$
(a) Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $A$.
(2)
When $t=2$, the velocity of $B$ is $(4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

When $t=5$, the velocity of $B$ is $(\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

(b) Find the acceleration of $B$, giving your answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.
(2)
(c) Find the velocity of $B$ at time $t=0$, giving your answer in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.
(2)
At time $T_1$ hours after noon, both boats are moving with the same speed.

(d) Find the exact value of $T_1$
(4)
At time $T_2$ hours after noon, both boats are moving in the same direction.

(e) Show that $3T_2^2+pT_2+q=0$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers to be found.
(3)
